elements.quote: Severe trauma is a major global public health issue [1]. ... Approximately 33% patients with TBI present with coagulopathy, which can increase the hemorrhage expansion and risk of death [4]. ... This systematic review aimed to assess the effectiveness and safety of systemic hemostatic agents as adjunctive treatment measures initiated in the pre-hospital setting and then continued in the in-hospital setting in patients with major trauma and hemorrhage or with TBI.
elements.reason: Describes current knowledge on trauma, coagulopathy, and mortality, and aims to assess effectiveness and safety, indicating important uncertainties.

elements.quote: A systematic review and meta-analysis was therefore conducted to assess the effectiveness and safety of systemic hemostatic agents as an adjunctive therapy in people with major trauma and hemorrhage or TBI in the context of developing the Italian National Institute of Health guidelines on major trauma integrated management.
elements.reason: Explains the importance and need for conducting the review to inform guideline development.

elements.quote: To our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive systematic review with a meta-analysis assessing the certainty of evidence by the GRADE approach to prove the efficacy of systemic hemostatic agents as an adjunctive treatment initiated in the pre-hospital setting among traumatic patients with (1) hemorrhage, (2) TBI, or (3) hemorrhage and TBI.
elements.reason: Explains the need for the current review by claiming it is the first comprehensive review with GRADE, addressing a gap despite existing similar reviews.

elements.quote: the benefits of TXA therapy seen in the first 3 h may be explained by the increasing levels of plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 and a reduction in fibrinolysis.
elements.reason: Briefly describes the proposed mechanism of action for TXA, a key intervention in the review.
No evidence of a logic model being considered or presented for complex interventions or delivery contexts in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: This systematic review aimed to assess the effectiveness and safety of systemic hemostatic agents as adjunctive treatment measures initiated in the pre-hospital setting and then continued in the in-hospital setting in patients with major trauma and hemorrhage or with TBI.
elements.reason: Explicit statement of review objective incorporating PICO-like elements
No explicit statement of planned comparisons using PICO in the objective statement

elements.quote: Two independent authors (A.B. and G.P.) completed reference screening and study selection using the following predefined inclusion criteria: (1) population : children, young people, or adults who have experienced a suspected hemorrhage or TBI following a traumatic incident; (2) intervention : administration of a systemic hemostatic agent, (e.g., rFVIIa, TXA, fibrinogen concentrate, prothrombin complex concentrate, or another anti-fibrinolytic agent); (3) comparison : no treatment, placebo, standard care (e.g., crystalloids, blood components), or any other hemostatic agent; and (iv) setting: systemic hemostatic treatment initiated in the prehospital setting. Only RCTs were considered eligible for inclusion; case reports, editorials, and letters were excluded from the search. When multiple publications for the same trial reported different outcomes or follow-up data, they were counted as a single publication.
elements.reason: Specifies study characteristics including PICO components, eligible study designs (RCTs), settings (pre-hospital), and follow-up requirements.
No evidence found specifying eligibility criteria for report characteristics such as dissemination year, language, or publication status.
The review does not appear to exclude studies based on outcomes not measured or not reported; eligibility is based on study design and PICO criteria.

elements.quote: Subgroup analyses were planned for (1) type of population (e.g., subjects with significant hemorrhage and subjects with TBI); (2) type of injury (e.g., blunt trauma, penetrating trauma); and (3) doses of systemic hemostatic agent when available.
elements.reason: Specifies groups used in syntheses, linked to comparisons defined in review objectives (e.g., population types).

elements.quote: Inclusion criteria were narrow, aiming to balance pros and cons. We considered eligible all RCTs that investigated several interventions delivered in any setting (civilian and military). Thus, although we were able to offer the highest level of evidence (RCTs with high certainty of evidence) achieving more consistency in the interpretation of findings, this approach limited the results as we did not find studies in military setting or studies involving fibrinogen concentrates, prothrombin complex concentrate, or other anti-fibrinolytic agents.
elements.reason: Rationale provided for restricting study eligibility to RCTs to ensure high certainty of evidence.

elements.quote: Our results are in agreement with those in the current scientific literature. Specifically, meta-analyses and systematic reviews conducted in the pre-hospital or the hospital setting found that TXA reduces the risk of death from all causes by about 20% [44, 53, 54] and less hemorrhagic expansion [44] among TBI patients [32, 46]; yet some results were discrepant with respect to functional status [32, 44, 54, 55].
elements.reason: The results are explicitly interpreted by comparing them to findings from other meta-analyses and systematic reviews, noting agreements and discrepancies.

elements.quote: This study has some limitations. First, survival bias may be present when patients die before the administration of treatment; thus, the results might not be generalizable across the trauma population [56].
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly discusses limitations of the evidence, including survival bias, misclassification, and heterogeneity.

elements.quote: The British Committee for Standards in Hematology recommends the administration of TXA in adult trauma patients with, or who are at risk of, bleeding as early as possible after injury [50], and the STOP the Bleeding Campaign in Europe also recommends its use in bleeding trauma patients within 3 h after an injury and those 'en route' to the hospital [51].
elements.reason: Explicitly discusses how results support existing practice guidelines for TXA administration.

elements.quote: On the basis of existing evidence, TXA was also included on the World Health Organization's list of essential medicine for the reduction of death among adult patients with trauma and a significant risk of ongoing hemorrhage [52].
elements.reason: Directly references policy implications, specifically WHO's inclusion of TXA based on evidence.
